h1: The 6 Best Self-Cleaning Robot Vacuum Mops of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Self-Cleaning Robot Vacuum Mops: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 robot vacuum mops with self-cleaning docks, from roborock and iRobot to Shark and eufy, scored on pad washing and upkeep.
summary: The roborock Qrevo S5V is the best self-cleaning mop for hard floors with lots of baseboard, thanks to its FlexiArm edge pad. The Roomba 505X wins on odor control with its hot-dry cycle. The Shark Matrix Plus is the cheapest true washing dock. The Tikom and Q7 L5 do not wash the mop at all.
intro: Most buyers read "self-cleaning" and assume the robot washes its own mop. Often the dock only empties the dust bin, and the pad is still your job. That gap decides whether you get a fresh-smelling floor routine or a damp pad festering in a closed base, which turns musty within a day or two.

Our ranking sorts six models by what the dock really does: wash the mop, dry it, handle the bin. Four wash the mop. Two are flagged as honest fallbacks. Scores come from spec sheets, manuals and owner feedback, then weighted for mop style, suction and price, so a bin-only dock never gets credit it has not earned. Treat the dock description, not the box art, as the deciding line.

products.name: roborock Qrevo S5V Robot Vacuum and Mop, FlexiArm Edge Mopping
products.verdict: A self-cleaning dock plus a mop arm that reaches the edges.
products.description:
The roborock Qrevo S5V pairs a self-cleaning dock with FlexiArm edge mopping, and it is the only pick here that attacks the usual weakness of round robots. A fixed pad leaves a grimy strip along baseboards and cabinet toes. The FlexiArm extends a pad toward the wall, so that strip actually gets wet. It sits in the $200 to $500 tier.

It tops the list because it solves two complaints at once: the dock keeps the pad clean, and the arm solves reach. The Roomba 505X beats it on drying, since the S5V lists no hot-air step, but the S5V is the stronger mopper where walls meet floor. Against the eufy C28, the arm matters more than raw suction on a mopping job.

Buy it for hard floors with long runs of baseboard. The caveat is footprint: the dock is large, and the extra arm is one more part to keep clean. Mostly carpeted homes should skip it.
products.idealFor: Hard floors with plenty of baseboard.

products.name: iRobot Roomba 505X Robot Vacuum & Mop Combo
products.verdict: The dock rinses the pads and finishes with a hot-dry cycle.
products.description:
The Roomba 505X is the answer to the damp-pad smell problem. Its multifunction dock empties the bin for up to 75 days, rinses the spinning pads, then finishes with a hot-dry cycle. Drying is what stops the sour odor that develops when a wet pad sits in a sealed base. The pads also lift when the robot rolls onto carpet, which protects rugs from a soaked pad.

It ranks second, not first, because it has no edge arm. Baseboards get less thorough coverage than with the S5V, which wins on reach. Against the eufy C28 and Shark Matrix Plus, though, it is the only one here that lists drying at all, so it is the cleanest long-term setup.

Buy it if odor is your reason for upgrading. The caveat is the bulky dock, which needs clear space on each side of it.

products.name: eufy C28 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 15,000 Pa, HydroJet Roller Mop
products.verdict: A roller mop with a self-washing dock and 15,000Pa suction.
products.description:
The eufy C28 swaps the pad for a HydroJet roller mop, and the dock washes that roller between runs. A roller is continuously rinsed against the floor, so it carries sticky residue off rather than smearing it around, which is why it suits syrup, juice and dried spills. The listed 15,000Pa of suction is also the highest figure in this roundup.

It lands third because it lacks two things above it. There is no edge arm like the S5V's, and no drying step like the 505X's. Against the Shark Matrix Plus, it brings notably more suction and a roller that sheds grime, so the premium is justified for a messy household.

Buy it for a family kitchen with frequent floor spills. The caveat is maintenance: the roller needs periodic checks, and no drying step is listed, so odor control depends on you.
pros: Roller mop washed at the dock

products.name: Shark Matrix Plus 2-in-1 Robot Vacuum & Mop, AV2613WA
products.verdict: A 2-in-1 that empties its bin and rinses its pad at the dock.
products.description:
The Shark Matrix Plus 2-in-1 is the cheapest route to a dock that genuinely washes the pad. It vacuums and mops in one pass, then returns to a base that rinses the pad and handles auto dirt disposal. Shark's Matrix navigation is designed to hold straight lines and reach corners and edges. It sells under $300, well below the three picks above it.

It ranks fourth because the savings come with gaps: no drying step is listed, no edge arm, and the mop specs are thin. The eufy C28 offers more suction and a roller, and the Roomba 505X handles odor. Against the Tikom below, this is the only mid-priced option here that actually rinses the pad.

Buy it for a mid-budget home that wants the dock to do the work. The caveat is how little the listing says about the mop itself.
products.idealFor: Mid-budget homes wanting a washing dock.
products.skipIf: You want the best mop reach.

products.name: Tikom Robot Vacuum and Mop, Robotic Vacuum Cleaner with Self-Emptying Base
products.verdict: A self-emptying base at a mid price, but you still wash the pad yourself.
products.description:
The Tikom is only half a self-cleaning robot. Its self-emptying base pulls dust out of the bin so you skip the daily trip to the trash, and app control handles scheduling. The mop, though, is not washed by the dock. You pull the pad and rinse it by hand, which is exactly the chore this guide is about.

It ranks fifth because every model above it washes the mop and this one does not. We include it as a budget step for households that vacuum far more than they mop. Against the Shark Matrix Plus, you save money and give up the rinse.

Buy it if dry vacuuming is 90 percent of your use and mopping is an occasional bonus. The caveats are an unfamiliar brand and sparse mop details. Skip it if the point of your purchase is a mop that cleans itself.
cons: Mop is not washed by the dock
products.idealFor: Homes that vacuum often and mop occasionally.
products.skipIf: You want the mop cleaned automatically.

products.name: roborock Q7 L5 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 8,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: Not self-cleaning, but the cheapest roborock combo with 8,000Pa.
products.description:
The roborock Q7 L5 is the honest fallback. It combines vacuum and mop with 8,000Pa of suction and roborock's navigation, and it costs the least here, in the $100 to $200 tier. There is no self-emptying base and no self-washing dock, so you empty the bin and wash the pad manually.

It ranks last because everything above automates at least part of the upkeep. Against the Tikom, you give up the self-emptying base. Against the Shark Matrix Plus, you give up the washing dock. What you keep is a competent roborock robot at the lowest entry price.

Buy it for a small home on a tight budget where a cheap robot beats a poorly built dock. The caveat is plain: there is no automation beyond the cleaning run, so skip it if hands-off care is your goal.
products.idealFor: Small homes on a strict budget.
products.skipIf: Automation is the point of your purchase.

whatMatters.factor: Does the dock wash the mop?
whatMatters.detail: Many listings use "self-cleaning" loosely. A self-emptying base only removes dust from the bin. A washing dock rinses pads or a roller with fresh water and drains the dirty water into a tank. The difference decides how often you touch a wet pad. On a listing, look for washing, mop wash or self-cleaning pads, not bin emptying alone.

A wet pad sealed in a dock grows a musty smell within a day or two, so drying matters more than washing. Hot-air drying, like the Roomba 505X's, removes the moisture that causes it. If a listing never mentions drying, as with the S5V and C28, plan to pull the pad occasionally. Search the bullets for hot dry or air dry.

A washing dock holds a clean-water tank and a dirty-water tank. A small tank means refilling or emptying every few runs, which erodes the point of automation. Mop-heavy homes feel this most. The capacity appears in the spec table, not always the headline, so compare it against how many rooms you mop and how often.

Mop pads should lift when the robot reaches carpet, or a damp pad soaks your rugs. The Roomba 505X lists lifting pads, while others rely on no-mop zones set in the app. If you have rugs, check for lifting pads or carpet detection in the bullets. Without either, you must draw no-mop zones yourself.

Washing docks are large, roughly the size of a small bin, and the robot needs clear space on each side to return. They also need an outlet nearby and, usually, water you can carry to the tank. Measure the intended spot with that clearance included before ordering. A dock that does not fit ends up in a hallway.

faq.q: What does self-cleaning mean on a robot mop?
faq.a: Usually that the dock washes the pad or roller with fresh water. Some listings stretch the phrase to cover bin emptying alone. The Tikom is a clear example: its base empties dust, but you still wash the mop.

faq.q: Do self-cleaning mops get rid of odor?
faq.a: Washing helps, drying matters more. The Roomba 505X adds a hot-dry cycle, which targets the musty odor of a damp pad left in a closed dock. The S5V, C28 and Shark list washing but no drying step.

faq.q: Is the roborock Qrevo S5V worth more than the Shark Matrix Plus?
faq.a: If edges matter, yes. The S5V's FlexiArm reaches baseboards that the Shark Matrix Plus cannot. For open floors with little trim, the Shark is cheaper and still washes its pad at the dock, so the S5V premium is wasted.

faq.q: How often do I refill the dock tank?
faq.a: It depends on tank size and how often you mop. Check the capacity in the spec table and plan on a refill every few runs. Frequent mopping in a large home empties the tank on a washing dock like the C28's faster than expected.

faq.q: Can self-cleaning mops go on carpet?
faq.a: They should lift the pad first. The Roomba 505X lists lifting pads, so rugs stay dry. Others, like the Shark Matrix Plus, may rely on no-mop zones in the app, so set those up before the first run on carpet.

faq.q: Do I still need to clean the dock?
faq.a: Yes. Rinse the dirty-water tank and wipe the wash tray every week or two, even on a self-cleaning dock like the S5V's. Skipping it lets residue build in the tray, and the smell comes back despite the automation.

finalTake: Pick the S5V when edges and baseboards are the complaint, and the Roomba 505X when musty pads are. The eufy C28 suits sticky kitchen floors, and the Shark Matrix Plus delivers a real washing dock for under $300. Treat the Tikom and Q7 L5 as bin-only fallbacks, and read each dock description before paying for the word "self-cleaning".
